blocks.text: Audience: developers who write docs with coding agents (repo-docs seed). Style: YC launch video — real pixels, no music, one CTA, ≤170 spoken words. Enemy named on screen: the line diff.

| Time | Screen | Narration |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:09 | A real `git diff` of an ADR: wall of red/green | Your agent just rewrote your design doc. Here's the diff: eighty lines of red and green. Did it do what you asked? You can't tell. |
| 0:09–0:17 | Cut to black text on white: "Git keeps the books on code. Nothing keeps the books on what agents write." | Proofpress is the version ledger for the docs your agents write — ADRs, design docs, PRDs. Versions, readable diffs, review. The agent pays the ceremony. You just decide. |
| 0:17–0:28 | Terminal: `pip install proofpress`, add skill, agent edits doc, version appears in localhost review page | Setup is one install and one skill. No new editor, no migration. Ask your agent to update a doc — it now has a version. Immutable. Rollback-able. |
| 0:28–0:44 | Split screen: git patch vs. semantic diff view (moved / rewritten / 3→5) | Same change, two views. Git: eighty lines of noise. Proofpress: one section moved, one paragraph rewritten, one number changed. And the agent's changelog is verified against the real diff — it can't oversell its work. |
| 0:44–0:54 | Comment on a block → agent revises → resolution; provenance link opens the session | See something wrong? Comment on the block. Your agent revises; the comment stays open until it's actually addressed. Every change links back to the conversation that caused it. Forever. |
| 0:54–1:00 | Logo + tagline + repo URL | Agents produce. You decide. The ledger remembers. Proofpress — Draft, Review, Approve, for agents. Open source. Link below. |

~165 words. Delivery notes: speak slowly (reviewers watch at 2×); today's date visible in the terminal beat as proof of life; narration never describes what's on screen — it adds the judgment layer on top.
Red-line check: no mention of versioning code files; no review-of-humans language; "git" appears only as contrast, never as target.
